q: In your own words, where does your data actually live, and what makes a copy count as a real backup?
teach: From the lesson: count the homes of a photograph that matters to you.
teach2: From the lesson, in Professor Kim's words: 'A backup is a second copy of a file, kept in a different place from the first, made so that losing the first copy is an inconvenience instead of a disaster.' Another way to hold the whole answer: your data lives in real places — your machine's storage and, when it syncs, servers elsewhere — and only a copy in a different place protects you when one place fails.
walk: Walk it through: (1) A saved file lives in your own machine's storage, and a synced file also lives on servers in data centres. (2) A second copy on the same machine shares the first copy's fate, so it is not a backup. (3) In your own words: data lives in countable physical places, and a real backup is a copy kept in a different place from the first.
